Office hours are by appointment: [email me](mailto:noah.buckley@tcd.ie) with a couple of times that suit you. If you're writing a capstone or MSc dissertation with me, start with [Doing political science research](teaching/research-guide/index.html), which collects the advice I end up giving every year.

## 2026--27

MT 2026

::: {.entry-body}
**[POU11011 Introduction to Political Science](teaching/pou11011/)**\
First-year lecture module. What politics is, what power is, why states exist and why some of them work; ideologies and identity; democracy, dictatorship and the grey zone; institutions; who gets what. The course site has the module outline, FAQ and slides.
:::
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-when}
MT 2026
:::
::: {.entry-body}
**POU33201 Authoritarianism**\
Third-year seminar. How dictatorships work: repression and co-optation, elections without democracy, information control, elite politics, and why some regimes fall while most don't.
:::
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.entry-when}
HT 2027
:::
::: {.entry-body}
**POU44172 Russian Politics**\
Final-year seminar. Russian politics from the Soviet collapse to the war in Ukraine, with the post-2022 transformation of the regime running through every week.
:::
:::

## Supervision

I supervise final-year capstone projects and MSc dissertations on authoritarian politics, Russia and the post-Soviet region, public opinion, corruption, and elections, mostly using quantitative methods. Please read the [research guide](teaching/research-guide/index.html) before we meet.

## Also taught at Trinity

- Russian Politics under Putin (MSc seminar)
- Varieties of Authoritarianism (MSc seminar)
- Comparative Politics A and B (second-year lecture modules)
- Russian Politics after Communism (final-year seminar)
- Public Opinion (final-year capstone)
